header.stance: 非農轉弱支撐短債，長端殖利率仍偏高

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 非農轉弱支撐短債，長天期美債未跟進

美國招聘週四明顯放緩，市場降低Fed即將升息的預期，短天期美債結束連續兩日跌勢，長債卻幾乎未受惠。2年期每日參考殖利率下降3個基點至4.14%，10年與30年期微升至4.49%、4.98%。6月非農僅增加5.7萬人，約為預估的一半，前幾個月增幅也遭下修。

市場將已完全反映的25個基點升息，由10月延後至12月，7月升息機率降至約20%。初領失業救濟金仍低、工廠出貨增加，使數據不至於過度悲觀。投資人降低的是短期政策急迫性，並未反映經濟活動突然崩落。日本10年期標售疲弱、長天期殖利率上升，也未替美債帶來支撐。

信用市場仍能融資，整體需求與個別風險的差別卻更鮮明。銀行已為大型媒體收購的大部分債務找到買盤，CoreWeave則因新的雲端競爭而跌價。Brightline動用準備金付息，買到時間但未解決重整。投資級發債愈集中於AI借款人，這些公司間差異也就愈重要。

SIFMA建議假日前固定收益市場美東14:00收盤。本文採用財政部每日序列，其時間標示為17:00，並非精確的14:00報價；下文股票、匯率與商品的最終數值，也包含其後交易。

## 非農使升息定價延後，殖利率曲線趨陡

6月非農增加5.7萬人，低於預估中位數11.3萬，前兩個月也下修。失業率降至4.2%，主要因勞參率大幅下降，並非招聘轉強。短率期貨把7月29日升息機率由公布前約33%降至20%。年底前25個基點升息仍已完全反映，但時點由10月移到12月。

漲勢集中短端。除了2年期下降3個基點，5年期也下降1個基點至4.23%，10年與30年期參考殖利率則各升1個基點。2年與10年、2年與30年利差各擴大4個基點至35、84。整週2、5、10及30年期仍上升5、8、9及12個基點；一個月變化則為上升9、5、2及下降1個基點。單次偏弱非農，只扭轉部分近期定價。

失業救濟金資料較不令人擔心。截至6月27日當週初領減少1,000人至21.5萬，四週平均降至22.2萬。續領增加2,000人至181.4萬，平均升至180.3萬。新增裁員仍有限，失業者找到下一份工作的時間卻可能拉長。

5月工廠訂單在4月增加5.3%後下降1.3%，出貨仍增1.6%、未完成訂單增0.6%、庫存增0.2%。訂單降低削弱需求加速的說法，並未顯示生產與待交貨業務全面萎縮。

實質殖利率解釋了長端為何未跟漲。10年期增加1個基點至2.26%，損益兩平通膨率維持2.23%；5年期實質殖利率升1個基點至1.99%，7年期維持2.11%，20年與30年期升2、1個基點至2.60%、2.79%。指標名目殖利率微升，不是通膨補償再起。勞動轉弱減輕眼前政策風險，中長天期仍面對新供給及海外殖利率上行。

### 資金焦點移往7月7日交割

4及8週期國庫券各標售約$850億。4週期最高得標利率3.605%，投標倍數2.72；間接、直接與交易商承接67.05%、3.75%、29.20%，最高利率分配比例46.77%。8週期為3.650%、投標倍數2.70，承接比例61.72%、3.90%、34.38%，最高利率分配比例53.99%。兩券均於7月7日交割。

對應次級殖利率各升4、3個基點至3.67%、3.72%。6週期降3個基點至3.67%，13至52週期則降3至4個基點，落在3.76%至3.95%。弱勢集中當日標售天期，並非假日前全面缺乏現金。

Fed美東16:30公布的H.4.1顯示，截至7月1日當週準備金平均$2.967兆，增加$155億，財政部一般帳戶減少$385億。附賣回增加，證券投資組合縮小。這是下一波交割前的流動性背景，在建議債市收盤時尚未公布。

## AI發債提高指數評級，也增加集中度

6月底AA−與A級債占美國投資級指數52%，高於2021年約46%，BBB占比則由46%降至41%。高評級科技發債改善評級組成，也使指數更依賴少數借款人。7月1日高評級利差僅74個基點，接近數十年低點。

2026年各幣別AI相關債已發行約$2,200億，比2025全年多62%。Amazon、Meta、Alphabet與Oracle占約$1,070億美元債，Nvidia與SpaceX 6月各發$250億，推升當月投資級發債紀錄。美國六大超大型雲端業者今年準備投入近$8,200億AI支出，市場面對的是持續籌資需求，而非一波已完成的交易。

強勁現金流降低眼前違約疑慮，部分負債卻遠長於設備的可能使用年限。Alphabet發行100年期英鎊債，Nvidia與SpaceX都有20年及30年期。SpaceX次級表現疲弱已在前一週出現；現在更值得注意的是，緊窄利差能承受多少重複供給，尤其競爭若改變AI基礎設施預期報酬。

CoreWeave提供了直接例子。Meta宣布競爭性雲端業務後，其歐元債兩日下跌近2美分至96.8，前月發行的$12.5億債殖利率升至10.25%。投資人重新評估的是個別公司的競爭地位，並非所有AI債都同幅調整。

### 收購融資、可轉債與替代幣別各有買盤

銀行已取得足夠需求，涵蓋Paramount Skydance收購Warner Bros.約$490億債務方案的大部分。投資級貸款討論在指標加250至275個基點，第二順位債預期美元殖利率比可比較歐元券高約1個百分點。提前找到買盤降低銀行被迫留債的風險，投資人仍須消化龐大的收購新增負債。

澳幣市場則提供另一條出路。前述上半年袋鼠債紀錄A$520億、約$360億之外，新增交易細節顯示Aroundtown 1月籌A$6億，較長天期成本低於可比較歐元市場。中國美元發債減少後，亞洲資金改變配置，投標需求常超過供給。較高澳洲殖利率吸引買方，發行人再透過換匯換息轉回所需幣別；即使沒有澳洲營運需求，也可能取得低於或接近本國的成本。

日本企業上半年可轉債¥1兆，為2004年以來同期最高。日本製鐵¥6,000億創日本單筆紀錄，JX先進金屬籌¥2,500億。許多交易零票息，在本地利率上升下，以股權轉換價值降低現金利息，但投資結果仍取決於股價與債權保障。

Brightline在前一天協商之後，有了實際付款更新：公司動用準備金支付7月1日優先市政與公司債利息，$9.85億通行權債持有人則把付息寬限展至7月15日，為$55億債務談判多爭取兩週。付款避免即刻違約，但消耗流動性，控制權與順位仍待處理。

美東14:00之後，Barclays撤回$9.6億Sound Physicians貸款，即使利差500個基點也未獲足夠需求，再融資可能以修改後條件重新推出。連同先前撤回的Shutterfly聯貸，顯示整體槓桿貸款有買盤，並不保證每家公司都能成交。

稍晚公司債基金參考值小幅上漲，LQD漲0.17%、HYG漲0.15%、JNK漲0.11%。溫和整體報酬之下，投資人承擔的收購、股權轉換、雲端競爭與鐵路重整風險，差異很大。

## 日本標售疲弱，限制全球長債受惠幅度

日本10年期標售投標倍數3.13，低於前次3.53及一年平均3.33。10年期殖利率上升7個基點至2.77%，20年期上升9.5個基點至3.76%。財政擴張與央行緩慢升息能否跟上通膨的疑慮，反映在較弱買盤。

政策利率已達1%、為1995年以來最高，市場仍認為10月前再升息機率逾60%。先前短觀2.6%的長期通膨預期支持這項討論。外資6月賣出¥3.12兆日債，為三年最多，央行購買減少、政府供給卻增加。如何吸引替代買方，成為比政策發言更直接的問題。

首相高市早苗目標在2040年4月起的會計年度，將名目GDP擴至$6.8兆，市場也等待可能暫停食品飲料消費稅的細節。措施可支持名目活動，但央行減少支撐時，如何融資同樣重要。本地殖利率提高，也改變日本機構投資海外債券的相對吸引力。

歐洲新資料對債市較溫和。前一天歐元區通膨由3.2%降至2.8%後，5月失業率維持6.2%，失業人數月減5.5萬、年減15.8萬。首季房價年增4.7%，慢於前季5.1%。通膨緩解並未伴隨勞動市場疲弱或家庭資產價格崩落。

Christine Lagarde依當時能源成本可能擴散的情況，為6月升息辯護，同時承認第二輪效應尚未出現。Philip Lane仍注意薪資、食品與服務，Olli Rehn與Martin Kocher則認為近期風險下降。討論已不那麼急迫，並非宣布衝擊完全結束。

英國央行委員Catherine Mann目前支持維持3.75%，但表示若通膨預期、能源成本、利潤率或薪資協商持續不利，可能需要積極升息。前次會議以7比2否決升息25個基點，較低油價並未移除她的條件式緊縮立場。

澳洲5月商品貿易由A$13.83億順差轉為A$30.18億逆差，出口下降6.9%、進口增加2.6%，非貨幣黃金出口減少35%是主要原因。資料在7月1日美東21:30公布，早於週四美國盤，顯示外部活動轉弱；但跌幅集中黃金，不宜直接讀成全面需求下滑。

## Fed定價轉緩支撐新興市場，擔保為敘利亞開啟融資

美國就業報告後，新興貨幣上漲，南非蘭特與匈牙利福林約升1%，多個拉美貨幣也走強，彭博美元即期指數在美國交易時段跌0.5%。眼前Fed升息機率降低，減輕美元借款人的一項壓力。

本幣債需求此前已改善。泰國、印尼、印度及馬來西亞6月政府債外資流入合計$82億，為逾兩年最高，較高本地利率支撐息收配置。美伊協議後，新興亞洲債券指數上漲0.2%，拉美指標卻下跌0.6%，能源成本與國內政策仍帶來不同結果。

敘利亞重建融資則仰賴擔保，而非廣泛主權信心。JPMorgan、卡達國家銀行與阿布達比商業銀行正安排約$70億五年期資金，用於電力及機場。QNB將提供保證，其最大股東是規模$5,800億的卡達投資局。海灣支持讓部分信用曝險不再直接落在戰後營運環境，工程執行、國家治理能力與制裁歷史仍須考量。

南韓說明高本地利率為何既能吸引資金，也限制借款人。6月通膨由3.1%升至3.2%，核心2.5%，強勁出口、弱勢匯率及房市壓力，使央行立場偏緊。外資可改善債券承接，並不代表國內政策負擔已減輕。

部分先前贏家則受估值限制。中美洲與加勒比海主權債2023年以來報酬逾40%，多數在面額之上，平均殖利率5.9%，低於新興投機級主權平均7.7%。評級上調、交易加深，以及巴貝多、巴哈馬與薩爾瓦多相關的債務及保育交換交易，支持了重估。部分投資人開始退場，因較低息收留下的財政與政治風險補償有限。

EMB稍晚參考值漲0.19%，在匯率反彈之外提供溫和債券報酬。土耳其與哥倫比亞等依賴外資的國家，仍對Fed重新轉鷹敏感。低油價改善進口國成本，卻削弱出口國收入。共同美元壓力減輕，本幣債、外幣主權債及擔保項目的風險仍不相同。

## 晶片再跌，美元轉弱、黃金走高

稍晚跨資產收盤不像非農落差所暗示的那麼防禦。S&P 500幾乎持平於7,483.24，Nasdaq 100跌1.61%，半導體跌5.44%，VIX卻降2.65%至16.15。科技賣壓在債市收盤前已出現，最終數值呈現的是集中跌勢，而非全面股票撤資。

美元指數跌0.52%至100.86，黃金漲1.09%至$4,112.70，符合Fed緊縮急迫性降低的方向。但黃金上漲不代表所有美債殖利率都下降，長端參考值仍微升，大盤與波動率也未顯示全面避險。

原油當日近乎持平，並非再次下跌。WTI漲0.16%至$68.69，布蘭特漲0.32%至$71.80，月跌幅仍有25.47%、24.41%，保留Fed與ECB官員提到的能源緩解。10年期通膨補償穩定，長端實質殖利率卻未隨較弱就業下降。

眼前政策交易比成長前景更清楚：招聘轉弱後，美元下跌、短債上漲；大盤持平與波動率下降，並未反映衰退。對固定收益更重要的後續，是AI修正是否開始影響已承壓公司之外的投資計畫與信用需求。

## 假日後接續服務業資料與附息債供給

美國7月6日美東10:00公布ISM服務業及紐約Fed全球供應鏈壓力指數，7日08:30有5月貿易、11:00有6月消費者預期調查，8日14:00公布6月16日至17日FOMC紀錄。服務業招聘與價格、物流成本及家庭預期，將協助區分持續放緩與單次非農偏弱。

財政部6日美東11:30標售$920億13週期、$790億26週期；7日有$900億42天期、$520億52週期及$580億3年期。8日增額發行$390億10年期，9日增額$220億30年期。除了先前7日交割的新券，這波還有9日國庫券、15日附息債交割。需求將顯示短端漲勢能否與大額供給並存，以及較高長端殖利率能否吸引買盤。

日本3日標售約¥3.8兆3個月券，7日約¥6,000億30年期，9日約¥2.5兆5年期。長債標售將接續疲弱10年期結果與外資賣出。歐元區生產者物價及零售銷售6日美東05:00公布。日本需求與歐洲內部價格，分別檢驗全球債市能從美國勞動轉弱獲得多少支撐。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Weak Payrolls Lift Short Treasuries, but Long Bonds Hold Their Losses

US hiring slowed enough to ease expectations of an immediate Fed increase Thursday, ending two days of losses in short Treasuries. Longer bonds barely benefited. The two-year daily reference yield fell 3 basis points to 4.14%, while the 10- and 30-year yields edged up to 4.49% and 4.98%. June payrolls rose just 57,000, roughly half the forecast, and revisions reduced the preceding months' gains.

The report shifted a fully priced quarter-point increase from October to December and cut the implied probability of a July move to about 20%. Low initial claims and growing factory shipments tempered the disappointment. Investors were taking urgency out of the near-term policy outlook, not pricing an abrupt collapse in activity. Japan's weak 10-year auction and rising longer yields offered little help to US duration.

Credit markets remained open, but the distinction between strong aggregate demand and individual risk sharpened. Banks had lined up buyers for most of a huge media-acquisition financing, while CoreWeave debt weakened on new cloud competition. Brightline paid coupons from reserves, buying time rather than resolving its restructuring. The concentration of investment-grade issuance in AI borrowers made those company-level differences increasingly important.

SIFMA recommended a 14:00 ET fixed-income close ahead of the holiday. Treasury's official daily series carries a 17:00 timestamp and is used here as the day's reference, not an exact 14:00 quote. Final equity, currency and commodity values below also describe the later part of the day.

## Payrolls Delay Fed Pricing as the Curve Steepens

Nonfarm payrolls increased 57,000 in June against a 113,000 median forecast, with downward revisions to the previous two months. Unemployment fell to 4.2%, but a sharp drop in participation explained the decline rather than stronger hiring. Short-rate futures reduced the July 29 hike probability from roughly 33% before the release to about 20%. A quarter-point move was still fully priced by year-end, now in December instead of October.

The relief was concentrated in shorter maturities. Alongside the two-year's 3-basis-point decline, the five-year fell 1 to 4.23%. The 10- and 30-year references each rose 1 basis point. Both 2s10s and 2s30s widened 4 basis points, to 35 and 84. The week still left two-, five-, 10- and 30-year yields higher by 5, 8, 9 and 12 basis points. Over a month, those changes were +9, +5, +2 and −1. One weak payroll report had reversed only part of the recent repricing.

Claims offered a less troubling labor picture. New applications fell 1,000 to 215,000 in the week ended June 27, and the four-week average declined to 222,000. Continuing claims rose 2,000 to 1.814 million, with their average increasing to 1.803 million. Layoffs remained contained while finding another job appeared to be taking longer.

Factory orders fell 1.3% in May after April's 5.3% increase. Shipments nonetheless rose 1.6%, unfilled orders 0.6% and inventories 0.2%. The order decline weakened the case for accelerating demand without showing a collapse in the production pipeline.

Real yields explained the long end's resistance. The 10-year rose 1 basis point to 2.26% and its breakeven held at 2.23%. Five-year real yields added 1 to 1.99%, seven years held at 2.11%, and 20 and 30 years rose 2 and 1 to 2.60% and 2.79%. The nominal benchmark increase therefore did not reflect renewed inflation compensation. Softer labor reduced immediate policy risk, while longer maturities still faced upcoming supply and rising yields abroad.

### Cash Demand Shifts to July 7 Settlement

The four- and eight-week auctions each raised about $85 billion. Four weeks stopped at 3.605% with 2.72 bid-to-cover; indirect, direct and dealer shares were 67.05%, 3.75% and 29.20%, with 46.77% allotted at the high. Eight weeks cleared at 3.650% with 2.70 coverage, allocations of 61.72%, 3.90% and 34.38%, and 53.99% at the high. Both settle July 7.

The corresponding secondary yields rose 4 and 3 basis points to 3.67% and 3.72%. Six weeks fell 3 to 3.67%, while 13 through 52 weeks declined 3–4 basis points to a range of 3.76%–3.95%. Cheapening was concentrated in the maturities being sold, rather than showing a broad holiday cash squeeze.

The Fed's H.4.1 release at 16:30 ET subsequently showed reserve balances averaging $2.967 trillion in the week ended July 1, up $15.5 billion, as the Treasury General Account fell $38.5 billion. Reverse repos increased and the securities portfolio shrank. The release described liquidity heading toward the next settlement cycle; it was not available at the recommended rates close.

## AI Supply Raises Index Quality—and Concentration

AA− and A-rated bonds made up 52% of the US investment-grade index at June-end, up from about 46% in 2021, while BBB's share fell to 41% from 46%. Highly rated technology issuance had improved that ratings mix. It had also made the index more dependent on a small group of borrowers, with high-grade spreads at just 74 basis points on July 1, near multi-decade lows.

Companies had issued about $220 billion of AI-linked bonds across currencies in 2026, already 62% more than in all of 2025. Amazon, Meta, Alphabet and Oracle accounted for roughly $107 billion of dollar issuance. Nvidia and SpaceX each sold $25 billion in June, contributing to record monthly high-grade volume. The six largest US hyperscalers were preparing nearly $820 billion of AI expenditure this year, so investors faced a continuing financing requirement rather than one completed wave of deals.

Strong cash flows reduced immediate default concerns, but some maturities stretched far beyond the assets' likely useful lives. Alphabet issued 100-year sterling debt; Nvidia and SpaceX included 20- and 30-year tranches. SpaceX's weak secondary trading was already familiar from the prior week's reports. The new question was how much repeated supply tight spreads could absorb, particularly if competition changed the expected returns from AI infrastructure.

CoreWeave supplied a direct example. After Meta announced a competing cloud business, its euro bond fell almost 2 cents over two days to 96.8. The yield on a $1.25 billion issue sold the previous month rose to 10.25%. Investors were reassessing a specific borrower's competitive position, not simply marking all AI debt the same way.

### Acquisition Buyers, Convertibles and Alternative Currencies

Banks had gathered enough demand to cover most of the roughly $49 billion package backing Paramount Skydance's Warner Bros. takeover. Investment-grade loans were discussed at 250–275 basis points over benchmarks; expected dollar yields on second-lien bonds were about 1 percentage point above comparable euro tranches. Early demand reduced the risk that banks would be left holding the financing, while investors would still have to absorb a very large new-money acquisition structure.

Australian-dollar funding offered another outlet. Beyond the first-half Kangaroo record reported previously—A$52 billion, or $36 billion—new detail showed how issuers were using the market: Aroundtown raised A$600 million in January and placed longer debt below its comparable euro cost. Asian bids often exceeded supply after the decline in Chinese dollar issuance redirected portfolios. High Australian yields attracted buyers, and cross-currency swaps let issuers convert proceeds back to their required currencies, in some cases lowering or matching home-market funding costs despite no Australian operating need.

Japanese companies issued ¥1 trillion of convertibles in the first half, the most for that period since 2004. Nippon Steel's ¥600 billion transaction was a national record, and JX Advanced Metals raised ¥250 billion. Many issues had zero coupons. With domestic rates rising, issuers could reduce cash interest by offering equity conversion value, though investors' outcomes remained tied to share performance and bondholder protections.

Brightline provided an actual payment update after the previous day's negotiations. It used reserves to pay July 1 interest on senior municipal and corporate notes. Holders of $985 million of access-rights bonds extended their payment grace period to July 15, adding two weeks for talks over the railway's $5.5 billion debt. The payments avoided an immediate default but used liquidity without settling control and priority.

After the 14:00 rates cutoff, Barclays withdrew a $960 million Sound Physicians loan when demand was insufficient even at a 500-basis-point margin. The refinancing could return on revised terms. Together with an earlier withdrawn Shutterfly syndication, it showed that broad leveraged-loan demand did not guarantee execution for every borrower.

Later listed credit references were modestly positive: LQD gained 0.17%, HYG 0.15% and JNK 0.11%. Those small gains coexisted with large differences in what investors were funding—an acquisition, a convertible, a new cloud competitor or a railway workout.

## Japan's Weak Auction Limits the Global Duration Relief

Japan's 10-year auction drew 3.13 bid-to-cover, down from 3.53 at the previous sale and below the 3.33 one-year average. The 10-year yield rose 7 basis points to 2.77%, and the 20-year gained 9.5 to 3.76%. The weak bid followed fiscal-expansion concerns and doubts about whether gradual BOJ tightening could keep up with inflation.

The policy rate was already 1%, the highest since 1995, but markets put the probability of another increase by October above 60%. The earlier Tankan's 2.6% long-horizon inflation expectation reinforced that debate. Foreign investors sold ¥3.12 trillion of Japanese bonds in June, the most in three years, while BOJ purchases receded and government supply increased. Attracting replacement buyers was becoming a more immediate issue than policy commentary alone.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi targeted nominal GDP of $6.8 trillion in the fiscal year starting April 2040. Investors also awaited details of a possible suspension of food and beverage sales tax. The proposals could support nominal activity, but their financing mattered to bondholders as the BOJ reduced support. Higher domestic yields also changed the comparison for Japanese institutions considering overseas bonds.

Europe's latest releases were less threatening to duration. After the prior day's euro-area inflation slowdown to 2.8% from 3.2%, May unemployment held at 6.2%; the number unemployed fell 55,000 from April and 158,000 over a year. First-quarter house prices rose 4.7% annually, slower than 5.1% in the preceding quarter. Inflation relief was not accompanied by a weak labor market or a collapse in household asset values.

Christine Lagarde defended June's rate increase on the information then available, when energy costs appeared to be spreading through the economy, while acknowledging that second-round effects had not materialized. Philip Lane remained attentive to wages, food and services; Olli Rehn and Martin Kocher saw less immediate risk. The discussion had become less urgent without declaring the shock fully resolved.

BOE policymaker Catherine Mann supported holding at 3.75% for now but said persistent inflation expectations, energy costs, profit margins or adverse wage negotiations could justify an activist increase. Her position followed a 7–2 vote against a quarter-point hike at the last meeting. Lower current oil prices did not remove that conditional tightening case.

Australia's May goods balance swung to an A$3.018 billion deficit from an A$1.383 billion surplus. Exports fell 6.9% and imports rose 2.6%, with a 35% drop in non-monetary gold exports accounting for most of the export weakness. Released at 21:30 ET July 1, the data were available before Thursday's US session. They pointed to softer external activity, although the concentration in gold cautioned against reading the headline as a broad demand slump.

## Softer Fed Pricing Helps EM; Guarantees Reopen Syrian Funding

Emerging currencies rallied after the US employment report. The rand and forint gained about 1%, several Latin American currencies advanced and the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index fell 0.5% during US trading. Lower odds of an immediate Fed hike eased one source of pressure on dollar borrowers.

Local bond demand had already strengthened. Foreign inflows into Thai, Indonesian, Indian and Malaysian government debt reached a combined $8.2 billion in June, the highest in more than two years. Expectations of elevated local rates supported carry. Since the US-Iran agreement, an emerging-Asia bond index gained 0.2%, while a Latin American gauge lost 0.6%; lower energy costs and domestic policies were producing different outcomes.

Syria's prospective reconstruction financing depended on guarantees rather than broad sovereign confidence. JPMorgan, Qatar National Bank and Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank were arranging about $7 billion of five-year funding for power and airport projects. QNB would guarantee the facility; its largest shareholder was the $580 billion Qatar Investment Authority. Gulf backing shifted part of the lenders' credit exposure away from the postwar operating environment, though construction, state capacity and the history of sanctions remained relevant.

South Korea showed why high local rates could both attract capital and constrain domestic borrowers. June inflation had risen to 3.2% from 3.1%, with core at 2.5%. Strong exports, currency weakness and housing pressure kept the BOK restrictive. Foreign purchases could improve bond-market absorption without implying that the domestic policy burden was easing.

Valuations limited the appeal of some recent winners. Central American and Caribbean sovereign bonds had returned more than 40% since 2023; most traded above par with an average yield of 5.9%, against 7.7% for EM speculative-grade sovereigns. Rating upgrades, deeper markets and debt-for-nature transactions involving Barbados, the Bahamas and El Salvador had supported the rally. Some investors were retreating as lower carry left less compensation for fiscal or political setbacks.

EMB's later reference gained 0.19%, adding a modest positive debt return to the currency rally. Dependence on external capital still left countries such as Turkey and Colombia sensitive to renewed Fed hawkishness. Lower oil improved importers' costs while reducing exporters' revenue. The common dollar pressure eased, but local debt, hard-currency sovereigns and guaranteed projects retained different risks.

## Chips Fall Again as the Dollar Weakens and Gold Rises

The later cross-asset closes were less defensive than the payroll miss alone might suggest. S&P 500 finished almost unchanged at 7,483.24, while Nasdaq 100 fell 1.61% and semiconductors lost 5.44%. VIX declined 2.65% to 16.15. The technology selloff was already underway before rates closed, but final values showed concentrated losses rather than a broad equity liquidation.

DXY fell 0.52% to 100.86 and gold rose 1.09% to $4,112.70, consistent with reduced urgency around Fed tightening. Gold's gain did not imply that all Treasury yields had fallen: the reference long yields remained slightly higher, and broad equities and volatility showed little sign of a generalized haven rush.

Oil was nearly flat on the day rather than falling again. WTI rose 0.16% to $68.69 and Brent 0.32% to $71.80. Their monthly declines were still 25.47% and 24.41%, preserving the energy relief cited by Fed and ECB officials. The stable 10-year breakeven fit that broader backdrop even as long real yields resisted the softer jobs report.

The immediate policy trade was clearer than the growth outlook. Dollar weakness and short-Treasury gains followed weaker hiring, while flat broad equities and falling volatility did not price a recession. For fixed income, the more consequential follow-through would be whether the AI correction began to change investment plans and credit demand beyond the firms already under pressure.

## Services Data and Coupon Supply Follow the Holiday

US releases resume July 6 at 10:00 ET with ISM services and the New York Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index. May trade follows July 7 at 08:30 and the June Survey of Consumer Expectations at 11:00. Minutes of the June 16–17 FOMC meeting arrive July 8 at 14:00. Services hiring and prices, logistics costs and household expectations will help distinguish a durable slowdown from one weak payroll report.

Treasury sells $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills July 6 at 11:30 ET. July 7 brings $90 billion of 42-day bills, $52 billion of 52-week bills and a $58 billion three-year note. Reopenings follow: $39 billion of 10-year notes July 8 and $22 billion of 30-year bonds July 9. In addition to the earlier issues settling July 7, the new sequence brings July 9 bill and July 15 coupon settlements. Demand will show whether the front-end rally can coexist with another large supply week and whether higher long yields attract buyers.

Japan auctions roughly ¥3.8 trillion of three-month bills July 3, about ¥600 billion of 30-year bonds July 7 and ¥2.5 trillion of five-year debt July 9. The long-bond sale follows the weak 10-year result and foreign selling. Euro-area producer prices and retail sales arrive July 6 at 05:00 ET. Japanese demand and European domestic-price data offer separate tests of how far global duration can benefit from the softer US labor outlook.
